absent: Locking, concurrency, and reentrancy rules for sampling, walking, override parsing, and early mapping.
Internals of the callchain consumer, unified unwinder, adapter routine, and per entry callback contract beyond forwarding.
System capability queries, vector length accessor, compatibility checks, thread register accessors, and current task guarantees.
Layout of override records, global register table, boot status flags, and how later stages consume overrides.
Exact alias spellings and canonical expansions, plus limits for malformed alias bodies and overlong tokens beyond truncation.
Firmware property accessors, cache maintenance effects, randomization disable query, and hardware randomness contract.
Virtual address constants, page protection encodings, table entry formats, level shifts, and contiguity sizes.
CPU feature queries for authentication and branch protection, relocation effects, frame patching, and table switch primitives.
Error handling for allocation exhaustion during table building and for invalid physical or virtual bounds.
Whether override filters run with preemption or interrupts controlled, and ordering against concurrent CPUs.

findings.text: Provides kernel callchain sampling for performance events. The routine takes a sampling context plus a register snapshot, ignores guest execution, and otherwise requests a stack walk for the current execution context. The consumer used for the walk is callchain_trace.
Guest execution produces no records from this sampling path. A guest state query gates the walk, with a positive result causing immediate return and no further action.

Generic architecture stack walking service accepting a per entry consumer with opaque cookie plus a target task and register snapshot. The implementation resists inlining and instrumentation, and forwards through an adapter to the unified unwinder.

The walker builds a small adapter record holding the original consumer and cookie, then invokes the underlying unwinder with a fixed adapter routine and a pointer to that record alongside the original task and register inputs.

Family of performance register helpers covering extended value lookup, full register value lookup, mask validation, ABI identification, and capture of user visible register state. Together they define how sampling observes general, special, and extended state.

Extended vector granule reporting is only meaningful when scalable vector support is present. Without that support the lookup warns once and yields zero. When present the result derives from the current task vector length converted from bits into units of sixty four bits. Unknown extended indexes also warn once and yield zero.

For snapshots taken in compatibility mode, three positions receive special translation. The architectural stack and link positions return the compatibility stack and link fields, and index fifteen returns the program counter. This preserves historical unwinding expectations for thirty two bit tasks observed by both thirty two and sixty four bit consumers.

Index bounds are checked against the extended maximum with a single shot warning and zero result on violation. Native stack and program counter positions return their dedicated fields. Indexes at or above the base maximum delegate to extended handling, while remaining indexes return the corresponding general register slot.

Reserved mask covers all bit positions at and above the base register count, leaving lower positions as valid sampling mask bits. The value is the bitwise complement of a low bit mask spanning the base count.

Mask validation clears the vector granule bit from the reserved set when scalable vector support exists. It then rejects an empty mask or any mask touching reserved bits with an invalid argument failure, otherwise reporting success.

ABI identification returns the thirty two bit variant for compatibility threads and the sixty four bit variant otherwise. User register capture fills the destination with the current task register area and the ABI derived from the current thread.

Feature override descriptor pairs a fixed size register name with a position independent reference to an override record and a trailing variable length field array. Each field entry holds a short name, a bit shift, a bit width, and an optional position independent validation hook returning a boolean decision. A helper macro builds four bit wide entries from name, shift, and hook.

Sizing facts for override metadata. Register name storage holds twenty characters, field name storage holds ten, alias storage holds thirty, and alias expansion storage holds one hundred sixteen. Field width defaults to four bits unless explicitly narrowed, including a one bit floating case.

Override tables exist for several identification registers plus a software feature pseudo register. Memory type tables cover extended control, virtualization and atomic flags, address range, and nested virtualization fraction. Processor feature tables cover vector, exception level, partitioning, branch, guarded control stack, tagging, matrix, and related fractions. Instruction set tables cover pointer authentication variants, wait with timeout, and move operations. Matrix tables cover version and floating support. Software tables cover randomization disable, hypervisor mode, and read only data control.

Virtualization host override is rejected when early boot state indicates execution in elevated mode with host extensions forced while requesting a disabled value. The check prevents forced non host mode on cores that require host mode.

Address range override only accepts the disabled value, with any enabled request refused. When disabling on systems with large address support, the logic also constrains related granularity and physical address range overrides to compatible values.

Disabling vector or matrix extensions also clears the associated supplemental feature override to all zeros with full coverage. This ensures dependent capabilities disappear together with their parent.
Hypervisor host extension software override is accepted only for the enabled value, when early boot mode is elevated, and when hardware reports host support. All other combinations are refused.

A small alias table maps friendly command line spellings to one or more canonical override assignments. Aliases cover hypervisor modes, single feature disables, grouped authentication disables, and options for randomization, read only data, atomic handling, address range, exception level, and partitioning. Alias expansion does not recursively expand further aliases.

Value parsing accepts an optional hexadecimal prefix followed by exactly one hexadecimal digit. Longer values, missing digits, or trailing non space characters cause failure. Letter digits are case insensitive.

Field lookup constructs the expected dotted assignment prefix from register and field names plus a separator, then compares against the input token. On prefix match the remainder is parsed as a value, otherwise the field is skipped.

Option matching scans all known registers and their fields for a prefix hit. When a filter hook exists and rejects the value, the override is marked as filtered by setting value bits and clearing coverage for that field. Otherwise the value bits are inserted and coverage is set. Successful insertion stops the scan.

Command line processing repeatedly skips leading blanks, stops at end of input or a standalone double dash terminator, and extracts the next blank delimited token with dashes normalized to underscores into a bounded buffer. Each token is offered to direct option matching and then to alias comparison, with alias bodies reprocessed without further alias lookup.

Feature override initialization first clears all stored values and coverage, records early boot status, then selects command line sources. A forced built in source uses only the embedded string, otherwise built in is used when no boot arguments exist and boot arguments are used when present. After parsing, each override record is flushed from cache to point of coherency.

Early entry for establishing identifier overrides from firmware description and boot status. It prepares override storage, consumes command line inputs, and ensures visibility to later stages through cache maintenance.

Early randomization entry deriving a kernel image displacement. It honors a command line disable, consumes a firmware provided seed when available, falls back to hardware randomness when needed, and otherwise disables displacement by returning zero.

Seed acquisition reads a single eight byte property from the chosen node, returns zero when the node is invalid or the property is missing or malformed, and clears the property after successful read to prevent reuse. Displacement places the image within the middle half of the available virtual range, offset from the base by half the half range plus a seed scaled fraction of that half range.

Recursive page table construction service for early mapping. It accepts a page allocator cursor, virtual bounds, physical base, protection attributes, nesting level, table pointer, contiguity permission, and address offset.

Bounds and base are page aligned before use, and the table cursor is advanced to cover the start. Empty protection clears mappings without setting block or page type, otherwise level determines block versus page encoding. Chunks requiring finer granularity allocate a new table when empty and recurse one level deeper. Contiguity hint is set when start and base share required alignment and permission allows, and cleared when remaining length cannot fill a contiguous unit. Physical base, virtual cursor, and table position advance together until the end.

Segment mapping converts kernel link addresses to table indices by adding a virtual offset and removing the direct map base, spanning from inclusive start to exclusive end with given protections and contiguity policy. Unmapping reuses the same path with empty protections and no contiguity.

Kernel image mapping proceeds through protection selection, initial mapping, optional second pass, and final table publication. Text starts read only executable and data as writable, with debugger override permitting writable text and guarded page marking when branch target protection is active. Shadow call stack is disabled when pointer authentication or branch protection is present. A second pass is required for relocatable images or when shadow handling is active, initially mapping code as writable. After barriers and a temporary table switch, relocation and frame patching occur with instruction cache maintenance, followed by text unmapping, TLB invalidation, and remapping with final protections and contiguity. The completed root table is copied to its final location with barriers and a final table switch.

Initial mapping treats a leading header plus read only and init data as non executable writable, main and init code with the selected code protection, and trailing mutable data as writable with contiguity allowed. Main code allows contiguity only on single pass flows. Remapping restores main code with final text protection and contiguity, and init code with final text protection without contiguity.

Position independent reference helper converts a stored relative descriptor into a usable pointer of the expected type, enabling early code to access override records and tables before absolute addressing is available.

Several paths warn once and substitute zero on unexpected conditions, including missing vector support, unknown extended indexes, and out of range register indexes. Command line token extraction truncates overlong tokens at the buffer limit without explicit error, and alias bodies are assumed to fit canonical option syntax.

Filtered overrides use a fragile encoding that sets value bits while clearing coverage, requiring consumers to interpret this combination as rejection rather than a real value. Early mapping expects no fresh table allocations during remapping phases, and requires explicit unmapping plus TLB maintenance before reestablishing contiguous text to avoid conflicts.

Randomization seed is cleared after consumption to prevent reuse, and cache maintenance is required after override updates for visibility. Missing seeds or randomness sources silently disable displacement rather than failing boot.
